summary: Bandai Namco's Wii resort-sports line, beginning with Balance Board skiing, expanding into skiing and snowboarding, then broadening into the multi-resort Go Vacation.

entries.title: Go Vacation
entries.definitive_edition: Nintendo Switch port, with Wii original as control-context secondary

emulation.emulator: Nintendo Switch hardware for primary; Wii hardware/Dolphin for original
emulation.notes: Use Switch for the recommended route; use Wii hardware or Dolphin for original accessory/control comparisons.
emulation.fidelity_ceiling: Nintendo Switch port for modern play; Wii original for accessory authenticity

primary.why: Go Vacation released for Wii in 2011 as a spin-off/third entry in the We Ski line, then was ported to Nintendo Switch in 2018 with new features such as animal photography and reward boxes. Switch is the most accessible and feature-expanded route, while Wii remains relevant for original motion/peripheral controls.
primary.how_to_play: Play the Nintendo Switch version for the modern feature-expanded route; use Wii hardware if preserving original Wii Remote, MotionPlus, Balance Board, Wii Wheel, or Wii Zapper-style control options matters.

secondary.why: Preserves the original control/peripheral context, including Wii-specific accessory support.
secondary.how_to_play: Play on Wii or Wii U with the relevant Wii controllers/accessories.

all_releases.fidelity: Original Wii release with Wii-specific accessory/control support.
all_releases.reason: secondary: preserves original motion/peripheral context not fully represented by the Switch port.

all_releases.fidelity: Modern port with new photo/reward features and improved accessibility.
all_releases.reason: primary: most accessible and feature-expanded route.

fidelity_vs_completeness_conflict.note: Switch has the modern feature-expanded route, while Wii preserves original controller and accessory support; use Wii as secondary for control-history completeness.

entries.remaster_caveats: Switch port adds new features; Wii accessory-dependent activities may feel different outside the original Wii setup.
